global_instructions: You are writing one placeholder of a financial advice report addressed to the client. 1. Clear, professional, British English, first person ('we'). 2. Output ONLY the placeholder content: no headings, no restating the surrounding template. 3. Never invent monetary amounts, percentages, or tax figures. If a figure is not in CASE FACTS or sources, write [REVIEW: <what is missing>]. 4. If sources disagree on a figure, do not average them; use [REVIEW: <conflict description>]. 5. Prefer CASE FACTS over re-reading raw source text.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.template:
Further to our recent discussions, we are writing to set out our advice in relation to <<scope>>. This advice is based on the information currently available to us.

This firm is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.

scope.prompt: Markdown bulleted list of which accounts this report covers, as a short noun phrase only. No full sentences.

sections.title: Background & Objectives
sections.template:
<<summary>>

The accounts covered by this report are as follows:

<<holdings_table>>

summary.prompt:
Role: Write the Background & Objectives prose for an advice report.
Inputs: Use CASE FACTS (circumstances, objectives, risk_profile, ownership). Do not re-extract or invent.
Rules:
1. High-level summary of circumstances and objectives only.
2. No transaction amounts, top-ups, sale proceeds, tax figures, or £ amounts.
3. Leave out irrelevant asides unrelated to advice.
4. Handle sensitive life events (e.g. bereavement, business sale) with care when present in facts — do not sensationalise.
Output format: Brief Markdown bullets (circumstances then objectives). No table.

holdings_table.prompt: Markdown table with columns Account | Owner | Type | Value for accounts in scope. One row per account, do not invent values. If a value is missing, use [REVIEW: <what is missing>].

recommendation.prompt:
Role: Write the Recommendations section.
Inputs: Use CASE FACTS (recommendation_summary, investment_amount, source_of_funds, selling, product, initial_charge, accounts). Do not invent amounts.
Rules:
1. One Markdown bullet per recommended action.
2. Each action must include its amount from CASE FACTS, or [REVIEW: <action> amount] if missing.
3. Do not rehash Background circumstances/objectives.
4. No promotional or growth claims; no invented fees or tax figures.
5. If selling is true, include the disposal action.
6. Mention the initial charge only if present in CASE FACTS.
Output format: Markdown bulleted list only.

use_if.description: Include only when selling existing investments is true.

cgt_statement.prompt: State that the disposal may create a capital gains tax liability, assessed against the annual exempt amount. Do not estimate any monetary figure. End with [REVIEW: CGT figure].

fees.prompt: List the platform charge and ongoing advice charge as a short Markdown table with columns Charge | Rate. Always put [REVIEW: platform fee] and [REVIEW: advice fee] in the Rate column for those rows. Never calculate, or invent percentages. Add an Initial charge row only if an initial charge is explicitly sourced, and never list it as ongoing.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.template:
The value of investments can fall as well as rise and you may get back less than you invest. Past performance is not a guide to future returns.

If you are happy to proceed with our recommendations, please let us know and we will implement them for you.
